name: Cleveland Clinic
notes: No RSS feed (/feed returns 404). The listing page is server-rendered and article URLs look like /YYYY/MM/DD/slug. robots.txt sets Crawl-delay: 10, which web.py respects. remove_selectors drops the 'for news media use only' notice and image captions. Terms say material 'cannot be reused without permission', so only an excerpt is stored.

name: Stanford Medicine
notes: No RSS feed or sitemap. all-news.html loads its list with JavaScript, but news.html has a server-rendered 'Latest Articles' list. The selector picks each card's headline link and skips its older 'Related' links. remove_selectors drops the media-contact box, which was otherwise mistaken for the author. robots.txt Crawl-delay: 7. Terms allow personal, non-commercial use only, so only an excerpt is stored.

name: Mass General Brigham
notes: The homepage list is built with JavaScript (only 4 links in the HTML), but article pages are server-rendered and robots.txt lists a sitemap, so discovery reads the sitemap, newest lastmod first (lastmod only decides which URLs to fetch; it is never used as a date). Pages declare canonical URLs on www.massgeneralbrigham.org, hence the parent domain. Dates come from the 'articlepublishdate' meta tag: the generic 'published-time' tag is the CMS re-publish time (e.g. 2026-09-03 for an article written 2026-05-20), so pages without articlepublishdate get no date. Image captions sometimes appear in the text: the obvious selector for them (div.body-copy-inline-media) also wraps real body text, so it is deliberately not used. Terms allow personal, non-commercial use only, so only an excerpt is stored.
